newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise sells first oil from new N.Sea field.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise sells first oil from new N.Sea field.

text.p: British independent exploration and production company Enterprise Oil Plc has sold the first cargo of crude oil from the Banff North Sea field which came onstream earlier this month, trade sources said on Monday.
The 725,000-barrel cargo, due to load in the first half of October, was sold to U.S. major Exxon on Friday for a premium of 30 cents a barrel over North Sea benchmark Brent, delivered to Rotterdam.
Dated Brent was valued at $21.95 a barrel on Friday.
Banff, located 200 miles east of Aberdeen, contains between 20 and 110 million barrels of oil and is operated by Conoco U.K. Ltd which has a 31.7 percent stake.

Enterprise owns 25.9 percent. Other partners are Ranger Oil (U.K.) Ltd with 26.2 percent, Hardy Oil and Gas plc with 12.4 percent, Amoco (U.K.) Exploration Co with 2.0 percent and Santos Europe Ltd with 1.8 percent.

Banff came on stream on September 14 when Conoco began six months of early production aimed at recovering oil and gas as well as gathering data for the full development of the field, scheduled for the first half of 1998.
The field, discovered in 1991, was brought onstream under the extended test just 10 months after receiving government consent.

Banff crude is pumped via a floating production system and exported on the 750,000-barrel capacity Stena Savonita shuttle tanker. It is expected to reach a peak of 35,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the first phase.
Trade sources said a further six or seven cargoes of the classic North Sea light low-sulphur style crude would be sold on the spot market during the early production phase.
"There's no storage at the field so production will have to stop until the shuttle tanker returns from delivering the cargo," said a trader familiar with the field's operations.
"We expect a cargo will load about once every 25 days."
